title: Building a Beat in Layers
description: Start with one sound, keep adding until the beat is huge, then pull it all back.

steps.title: Building up, pulling back
steps.description: A song feels like it's going somewhere when the drums change with it. A common trick is to start with very little and add one sound at a time, so each new layer makes things feel bigger. Then, right when it's at its fullest, you drop most of it away. That contrast is what makes the big parts feel big.

steps.title: Just the kick
steps.description: Start with just the kick. On its own it's a bare pulse, the kind of thing you'd hear at the very start of a track.
steps.hint: Just KCK, the red pad top left.

steps.title: Add the hi-hat
steps.description: Add the closed hi-hat to the kick. Now there's something ticking along between the thumps, so it starts to feel like a rhythm.
steps.hint: Kick and closed hi-hat (CHH) together. Both are on the top row.

steps.title: Add the snare
steps.description: Bring in the snare. With kick, snare and hi-hat, you've got a complete basic beat.
steps.hint: The first three pads on the top row, all together.

steps.title: Open the hat
steps.description: Now swap the closed hi-hat for the open one. Same beat, but the ringing hat makes it feel louder and busier.
steps.hint: Kick, snare and OHH, the last pad on the top row.

steps.title: Everything in
steps.description: Throw in the crash too: kick, snare, open hi-hat and crash. This is the peak, the moment everything's been building to.
steps.hint: The same three as before, plus CRS on the bottom row. Close together in time is enough.

steps.title: Drop it all
steps.description: Now strip it right back to just the ride. After all that noise, one quiet cymbal feels like the room just opened up.
steps.hint: Just RDE, in the bottom right corner. Hit it gently if your controller responds to velocity.

steps.title: Making it grow
steps.description: You want the drums to build energy as a song goes on. What's the best approach?

quizOptions.label: Add more sounds, one layer at a time
